discovery: First horizon-scale images of black holes (M87* and Sgr A*) via Earth-sized very-long-baseline interferometry

nominees.name: Sheperd S. Doeleman
nominees.affiliation: Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

nominees.name: J. Anton Zensus
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany

subfield: Astrophysics / black hole physics and radio interferometry
motivation: Stellar orbits established that a compact object of four million solar masses sits at the Galactic Centre, but they could not image the horizon itself. The Event Horizon Telescope did. Falcke predicted in 2000 that a black hole 'shadow' would be visible at millimetre wavelengths. Doeleman led the decade-long 1.3 mm VLBI program that first detected horizon-scale structure in Sgr A* (2008) and built the EHT collaboration. Zensus's leadership in millimetre VLBI and his founding role in the collaboration made the global array possible. Their images of M87* (2019) and Sgr A* (2022) showed rings whose sizes match general-relativistic predictions for the independently measured masses, and polarimetric, multi-year data have since confirmed that the rings persist. The technology is new, the measurement is extraordinarily hard and repeatedly checked, and it turned a theoretical picture into direct observation. It has opened strong-field gravity near horizons to imaging.
